title: Takes a few days, but then 100% super effective!
date: Reviewed in the United States on December 9, 2025
review: Takes a little patience and understanding, but wonderful. At first it seems anti-helpful. Since it attracts fruit flies to be trapped, for a while you will see MORE fruit flies. I'd say essentially no flies after maybe three days, or just an occasional fly. Take the top off and look inside, you see nothing, but look inside with a FLASHLIGHT and you see thousands of dead ones on the bottom. My guess is that it takes a few days to fully interrupt the fly breeding cycle.

title: Doesn’t work one bit!!! Don’t buy!

review: Doesn’t work one bit. Gave it a shake, opened and the fruit flies just keep swarming on it or around it. Left it out and open even without the cap and the only thing it did was leave a musk in the air and it leaks through the rim. Don’t waste your money on this

title: Do your part and this product works.
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 1, 2026
review: Worked for me!Attack gnats at the source. Gnats and fruit flies love garbage, fruits, food, and water sources. Get rid of those things and the wondercide will work. Take out trash and clean thoroughly especially the sink (do not leave dirty dishes or water in the sink) Make sure the water in the drain (p trap) is not suitable for the fruit flies by leaving soap or bleach in it. Or just pour boiling water in it from time to time.I will say I had to supplement with cleaning of the sink with a lot of dish soap and the drain. I made sure I kept the sink clean, left bleach in the drain overnight or for hours, and stored the canister of wondercide next to my produce (fruit) on the counter. I recommended this for a friend and they had different results. (I'm not sure if my friend did the same thing/ also they had pets) Also I would sometimes pour boiling water in the sink from time to time without bleach.Another easy way to get gnats down was to use a lot of dish soap to clean the sink and make sure it got bubbles and bubbly in the drain.I will also note that I did the cleaning with the bleach in the drain without the wondercide and the gnats stayed. It wasn't until I did everything with the wondercide that it worked and continued to work for months (I didn't have to keep up with the bleach in the drain and cleaning aggressively. I only did this initially)Bottom line: do your best to get rid of the gnats by yourself with the product OR use this product and continue like you would normally try to get rid of the gnats. Once you get rid of the gnats keep this product by your fruits, near the sink or just in the kitchen and you won't see gnats for months. If the flies return later check the canister and replace it. *Also I used one canister at a time. I hope this helps!***Some people may feel like this is too much but I don't think there is a miracle product for gnats and fruit flies. If there is an old banana and a trap the flies will simply go to both. That's why you have to do some work and use a trap.

title: Doesn't trap and kill
date: Reviewed in the United States on June 16, 2025
review: It attracts them for sure but doesn't work to trap and kill. My homemade traps work more effectively than these but I thought I'd give these a shot to save time. The insects just fly to it and hang out. They've been sitting there for 2 weeks with little to no difference.

title: Strong odor
date: Reviewed in the United States on March 27, 2026
review: Seem to work pretty well, but strong odor can spread thru room.

title: Underwhelming
date: Reviewed in the United States on April 26, 2024
review: First off, the description says that this is supposed to be a 2 pack, but we only received one trap. $22 for one trap is definitely not worth it.So far, after using this for several days, the results have been underwhelming. We have had better results using plastic containers with apple cider vinegar and a couple drops of dish soap, topped off with some plastic wrap and a rubber band.These seem to attract the fruit flies, but as other reviews have stated, they don't actually go into the holes. I'm not sure if there's something that attracts them, but keeps them from wanting to taste the liquid, but it's been frustrating to witness - again - after spending $22, and not even receiving the full order to begin with.Giving it 2* because the design is promising and we'll probably test out the container with the apple cider vinegar and dawn dish soap mixture.

title: Buy these, they work!
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 17, 2026
review: This is our 3rd purchase and they really work! We had a tough time getting rid of some fruit flies a year or so back and this is what finally cleared them. They came back again this year and after we cleaned up and put the fruit away, these little containers did their job. I like them because they are small enough to hide behind other items and don’t stand out so much. They also don’t smell so that’s also a plus.

title: A good product for keeping fruit flies under control
date: Reviewed in the United States on August 12, 2024
review: The Wondercide Fruit Fly Trap is a solid solution for dealing with fruit flies in the kitchen and indoor areas. I noticed a significant reduction in the number of fruit flies within just a few days of setting it up. The trap is easy to use and has a pleasant, non-toxic formula, which is important to me since I have pets at home. The design is discreet and doesn’t take up much space, so it blends in nicely with my kitchen decor. The only reason I’m giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is that I found it slightly less effective in larger areas, but it works great in smaller, concentrated spaces. Overall, it's a very good product for keeping fruit flies under control, and I would recommend it to anyone dealing with this common issue!
